newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent firms on Nigeria, technicals.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent firms on Nigeria, technicals.

text.p: IPE Brent crude oil futures were firmer on Tuesday on technical factors and Shell Nigeria's declaration of force majeure on exports of Bonny crude oil because of a strike, traders said.
June Brent crude was 23 cents a barrel firmer at 1004 GMT at $18.57, while May gas oil was $1.25 up at $165.75 a tonne.
"It is up because of technical factors and on the fundamentals of this news," one IPE broker said.
"It had already broken through $18.50 so the news from Nigeria has only added six cents or so," one broker said, adding that there had been strong buying on the front spreads.
The $18.50 level was roughly the high point reached on a number of occasions this month and is the top of a recent gap on the spot continuation chart.
Technical analysts said that $18.77 was the most important number to watch on the upside now as it lies at the top of a gap on the June contract chart formed on April 2 and 3.
Chartists also said May gas oil futures would find it hard to break above $166/$166.50 a tonne, corresponding roughly to the highs of the latest trading range.
World oil prices strengthened on Monday amid news that Iraq was planning to breach a U.N. no-fly zone.
"Iraqi flights of returning pilgrims in breach of the U.N. no-fly zone scared participants and resulted in players being wary of wanting to sell," MeesPierson said in a daily report.
"This, combined with a rumoured squeeze of May delivery (last day today) into New York, gave good all round support to the markets," Mees Pierson said.

Independent forecasters Weather Services Corp. said in their three to five day weather forecast: "...mostly fair, seasonable to cool across the northern areas" of the U.S., "seasonable" in western Europe and "near to below normal" in Mediterranean Europe.
The Singapore Monetary Exchange (SIMEX) launched on Monday its revised 3.5 percent sulphur fuel oil futures contract. The opening trade was conducted at $98.00 a tonne.
